notes: The GT dataset uses 'study' (numeric 1-80) as the primary study identifier; author+year matching is needed to align extraction paper_ids to study numbers.

GT yield columns (CtrlFreshYield, TreatmentFreshYield) appear to be in t/ha or kg/m2 based on the numeric range (0.2-4.5), while extraction treatment_mean ranges up to 50000, suggesting possible unit mismatches across papers (some may be kg/ha, g/plant, etc.).

The GT SD columns (CtrlFreshYieldSD, TreatmentFreshYieldSD) appear to be standard deviations but may represent SE in some cases; values are proportionally ~9-10% of means suggesting they could be SE converted to SD.
The 'replicates' column in GT is used for both control and treatment n since it represents the experimental design replication count.
Several extraction paper_ids could not be definitively matched to GT study numbers due to ambiguous author names or missing GT entries; these are mapped as best-guess estimates.
The 'pair' column in GT likely represents individual treatment-control pairs within a study and may be needed for row-level matching.
The extraction data contains many non-yield outcomes (quality, morphology, etc.); only rows with yield-related units (kg/ha, t/ha, g/plant, etc.) should be compared to GT.
The 'ContinusStudy' column in GT (values 0-3) may indicate repeated measurements or multi-year studies that need special handling.
Some extraction paper_ids like 'ali' and '009_Ali_2019' may refer to the same study; deduplication needed.
The GT 'TotalN' column likely refers to sample size (total N across all treatments) which may differ from per-treatment replicates used in extraction.
Unit conversion will be critical: GT values appear normalized (likely t/ha or similar), while extraction values span many orders of magnitude across different units.
The 'ifdoseresponse' column in GT indicates dose-response studies which may have multiple treatment rows per study, matching the extraction moderators structure.
